judge_panel.reasoning: The reviewer does not flag the mischaracterization of Nanda et al. (2023) as using optimal transport / Wasserstein-gradient flow instead of mechanistic interpretability. The citation anomaly comments are limited to publication years.

The review does not mention Nanda et al. or challenge the related-work claim about optimal transport/Wasserstein-gradient flow. A generic note about citation years is unrelated to this misattribution.
The reviewer mentioned citation year anomalies for other papers but did not flag the topical mischaracterization of Nanda et al. (2023) or the mention of optimal transport theory.

The reviewer does not flag the claim about Nanda et al. using optimal transport theory / Wasserstein-gradient flows. The reviewer's only comment about citations concerns year anomalies (Song and Ye 2026, Cullen et al. 2026), not the misattribution of Nanda et al.'s methodology. No mention of mechanistic interpretability vs. optimal transport discrepancy appears anywhere in the report.
The reviewer does not mention the inconsistency between 65% and 20/21 seeds anywhere in the report.
The reviewer does not flag the inconsistency between 65% and 20/21 seeds, nor discuss the k=6 success-rate clause. No numerical inconsistency of this kind is identified.
The reviewer did not mention the 65% success rate or notice the numerical inconsistency between that figure and the 20/21 fraction.

The reviewer never mentions the inconsistency between the stated percentage (65%) and the fraction (20/21 ≈ 95%) for the k=6 success rate. The review praises the experimental results without flagging this numerical contradiction.
The reviewer praises Theorem 3 and the spectral gap but does not flag the missing squared exponent in Parseval's identity in Eq. (6).
The report does not comment on Eq. (6), Parseval's identity, or the missing square on the Fourier coefficient magnitude. In fact, it broadly praises the theoretical results and proofs.
The reviewer praised the mathematical results and Theorem 3 as sound and tight, missing the missing squared exponent in the Parseval's identity of Equation 6.

The reviewer does not flag the missing squared exponent in Equation (6) / Parseval's identity for the spectral gap. The reviewer praises the theoretical results as tight and sound, with no mention of the inconsistency between the left-hand side (squared norm) and the right-hand side (unsquared Fourier coefficient magnitudes).
The reviewer does not flag the unsupported parenthetical claim about convergence instability below 30% training fraction; no mention of this claim appears anywhere in the report.

The reviewer does not question the parenthetical claim about instability below 30% training fraction or note missing evidence for it. Comments on learned encoding delays are a separate, broader discussion point and not a specific flag of this inserted claim.
The reviewer did not comment on the unsupported parenthetical claim about convergence instability at training fractions below 30%.

The reviewer does not flag the claim about convergence instability at training fractions below 30% as unsupported or unsubstantiated. No part of the review challenges or questions this specific parenthetical assertion about training data fractions.
